cases.name: wal_write_readback_and_checkpoint
cases.observed: A synthetic WAL transaction committed two rows; a second SQLite connection read them; TRUNCATE checkpoint completed without a busy writer.

cases.name: actual_wal_and_shm_open_pinned_before_native_use
cases.observed: The open hook pinned WAL wal_object_1 at 0 bytes and SHM shm_object_2 at 0 bytes before returning each actual descriptor; WAL contained 8272 bytes before checkpoint; the matching MAP_SHARED call used the pinned SHM object, which grew to 32768 bytes. The WAL pin remained stat-able at 0 bytes after SQLite close.

cases.name: second_connection_shared_node
cases.observed: A second simultaneous connection completed a WAL read/write while the process observed only one physical SHM open; this is consistent with the pinned generated-code shared-node reuse path, not evidence of a per-connection owner callback.

cases.name: denial_cancellation_and_fresh_retry
cases.observed: Not exercised: this probe only demonstrates ordering with an allow decision; the global raw syscall hook is not a trusted authorization integration.

limitations: This standalone process installs raw generated xSetSystemCall callbacks; they mutate a package-global table and are not a supported per-VFS authorization API.
Only one synthetic database is used. Denial, cancellation, fresh retry and multiple-connection owner coverage are not exercised by this positive ordering probe.
The probe uses private generated ABI layouts and callbacks; it is not production integration or a supported driver contract.
It does not establish protected-owner inventory, revocation, worker lifecycle, external-writer coordination, other architectures or strict path containment.
